claims.text: Template-assisted atomic layer deposition combined with sacrificial template removal can produce noble-metal-based HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The proposed route provides better atomic precision than conventional synthesis methods.
The proposed route provides better control of complex surface structures than conventional synthesis methods.
Noble-metal precursors are deposited on a three-dimensional sacrificial template.
An inert processing atmosphere helps ensure accurate atomic incorporation.
Step-wise temperature control helps ensure accurate atomic incorporation.
An inert atmosphere and step-wise temperature control preserve the three-dimensional architecture.
The sacrificial template defines the initial three-dimensional morphology.
The sacrificial template guides atomic deposition.
Atomic layer deposition enables layer-by-layer deposition with atomic precision.
Template-directed deposition forms a three-dimensional framework.
Removing the sacrificial template yields a nanostructured HEA with controlled composition.
Removing the sacrificial template yields an HEA with complex surface features.
The resulting noble-metal-based HEA nanoframework exhibits uniform atomic mixing.
The resulting nanoframework exhibits precise control over its nano-architecture.
The resulting nanoframework has enhanced catalytic surface features.
Conventional high-temperature or bulk-melting HEA synthesis generally provides less control over morphology.
Conventional high-temperature or bulk-melting HEA synthesis generally provides less control over atomic distribution.
The effectiveness of the method may depend on sacrificial-template fidelity, maintenance of an inert atmosphere, and suitable temperature steps.
The scalability and adaptability of the method to different noble-metal combinations remain unvalidated.
